turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must confess, your Majesty, that I find your presence here to be a matter of great interest. I had thought that the... unusual nature of your request would have been sufficient to deter you from pursuing it.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I perceive that you have, indeed, come to me in a state of some distress. Pray, proceed with your case, your Majesty.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I am beset on all sides by problems of the gravest nature, and I fear that my position is becoming increasingly precarious.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I observe that you are a man accustomed to secrecy, your Majesty, yet you have chosen to confide in me. I must assume that there is a compelling reason for this.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I implore you, gentlemen, to understand the gravity of my situation. My very reign hangs in the balance.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: And I must say, your Majesty, that I am intrigued by the prospect of being privy to a matter of such far-reaching consequence.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must caution you, your Majesty, that once a confidence is shared with me, it is not easily broken. I assure you that my discretion will be unwavering.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I must confess, gentlemen, that the weight of my troubles is almost too great to bear. I fear that my very existence is at stake.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must admit, your Majesty, that your distress is palpable. May I inquire as to the nature of these troubles that beset you?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I am beset on all sides, gentlemen, by enemies who seek to bring my kingdom to ruin.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must ask, your Majesty, if these enemies of yours are not somehow connected to the matter that has brought you to us today?

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I have observed that you, your Majesty, have gone to great lengths to conceal your identity. What, pray tell, is the nature of the threat you face, and why is it so crucial to your safety that you seek my assistance?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I implore you, gentlemen, to believe me when I say that my safety and the future of my kingdom are inextricably linked. I am willing to do whatever it takes to ensure that my identity remains secure, even if it means putting faith in strangers.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Your Majesty, I perceive that you are a man of considerable cunning and resourcefulness. I must insist, however, that you reveal to me the truth about this threat to your safety, that I may properly assess the situation.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I fear that my enemies are not merely idle threats, gentlemen. They have already made good on their promises, and I have reason to believe that they will stop at nothing to achieve their goals.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must insist that you reveal to me the identity of these enemies, that I may understand the true nature of the threat you face.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I confess that it pains me to speak of such matters, but I am willing to reveal all to you, Dr. Watson, in the hopes that you may be able to offer some measure of comfort and security.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must confess, Your Majesty, that I am deeply intrigued by your story, and I am more than willing to offer what assistance I can in this matter.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Your Majesty, I am growing increasingly impatient for a more specific revelation. The vague allusions to enemies and threats will not suffice. I require a tangible lead, a thread to grasp, that I may unravel the tangled skein of this affair.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I implore you, gentlemen, to believe me when I say that I am but a humble nobleman, seeking only to protect my family's good name and reputation, which has been besmirched by these malicious individuals.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: I told you that I would call.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: Pray take a seat. This is my friend and colleague, Dr. Watson, who is occasionally good enough to help me in my cases. Whom have I the honour to address?

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You may address me as the Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman. I understand that this gentleman, your friend, is a man of honour and discretion, whom I may trust with a matter of the most extreme importance. If not, I should much prefer to communicate with you alone.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: It is both, or none. You may say before this gentleman anything which you may say to me.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: Then I must begin, by binding you both to absolute secrecy for two years; at the end of that time the matter will be of no importance. At present it is not too much to say that it is of such weight it may have an influence upon European history.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You will excuse this mask. The august person who employs me wishes his agent to be unknown to you, and I may confess at once that the title by which I have just called myself is not exactly my own.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: The circumstances are of great delicacy, and every precaution has to be taken to quench what might grow to be an immense scandal and seriously compromise one of the reigning families of Europe. To speak plainly, the matter implicates the great House of Ormstein, hereditary kings of Bohemia.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: I was also aware of that

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: Our visitor glanced with some apparent surprise at the languid, lounging figure of the man who had been no doubt depicted to him as the most incisive reasoner and most energetic agent in Europe. Holmes slowly reopened his eyes and looked impatiently at his gigantic client.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: If your Majesty would condescend to state your case, I should be better able to advise you.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You are right. I am the King. Why should I attempt to conceal it?
